about.title: Cerritos Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Cerritos sits at a crossroads of warehousing, retail, and light industrial activity near the SR-91 and I-605 corridors, which means workplace injuries here range from forklift accidents in distribution centers to falls at retail construction sites along Artesia Boulevard. Under California law, workers' compensation is typically the only path against your employer regardless of who caused the accident, but that's not always the full picture. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury, you may have grounds for a separate third-party claim alongside your work comp benefits. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; instead, we connect injured workers in Cerritos with independent attorneys who can walk through the details of your situation, explain your reporting deadlines, and help you understand whether a third-party claim might apply. There's no cost to you for this connection, and no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Workers in Cerritos Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Understanding the Third-Party Angle
items.desc: While workers' compensation is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker may still be liable. An independent attorney can help you evaluate whether that applies to your case.

items.title: Knowing Your Reporting Window
items.desc: California requires you to report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, and missing that window can complicate your claim. We connect you with attorneys who can explain what documentation and timing matter most.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: Retaliation for reporting an injury or filing a claim is illegal in California. If you're worried about your job security, an independent attorney can help you understand your protections before you take any next steps.

items.question: Can I file a claim if I was hurt on I-605 or the SR-91 corridor while working?
items.answer: Possibly, yes. If you were injured in a vehicle collision while performing job duties near these corridors, you may have both a workers' compensation claim and a separate third-party claim against another negligent driver. An independent attorney can help sort out which paths apply to your situation.

items.question: Does workers' compensation stop me from suing my employer?
items.answer: In most cases, yes, workers' compensation is the exclusive remedy against your employer regardless of fault. However, if someone other than your employer contributed to your injury, such as a subcontractor or equipment manufacturer, you may still have a separate claim against that third party.

items.question: What if my employer retaliates after I report an injury?
items.answer: Retaliation for reporting a workplace injury or filing a workers' compensation claim is illegal in California. If you believe you've faced retaliation, an independent attorney can review the details and explain what protections and options may be available to you.
